name: Conquian
description: Conquian is widely regarded as the ancestor of all Rummy games, originating in Mexico in the 19th century. It is a 2-player draw-and-meld card game played with a 40-card Spanish deck (8s, 9s, and 10s removed from a French deck). Players take turns forcing the opponent to take offered cards or themselves draw from stock, building melds of 3+ in sequence or of a kind. The first player to meld their entire 10-card hand wins.

history.origins: Believed to have originated in Mexico in the 1800s, possibly adapted from Chinese Mahjongg or from an earlier European game. It is considered the root ancestor of Gin Rummy, Oklahoma Gin, and all modern Rummy variants.
timeline: 1800s: Documented in Mexico as 'Conquian' or 'Con Quien'.
1900s: Influenced the creation of Rum (Rummy) in the USA.
Present: Played in Mexico under its traditional name; studied as the Rummy progenitor.
history.cultural: A foundational game of Mexican card culture and the documented ancestor of the entire Rummy family. Important in the history of card game taxonomy.
history.evolution: Conquian introduced the core Rummy mechanic: draw one card, meld if possible, discard. Its unique 'forced take' mechanicâ€”where you can compel your opponent to meld a discardâ€”is preserved in almost no other modern game.

setup.deck: 40 cards: Standard 52-card deck with 8s, 9s, and 10s removed. Rank order: A-2-3-4-5-6-7-J-Q-K.
setup.dealing: 10 cards each. Rest is stock. No initial discard pile.

rules.objective: Be first to meld all 10 cards (hands meld face-up; you keep some in reserve for sequences).
rules.gameplay:
The non-dealer offers (turns face-up) the top stock card:
- If the active player CAN incorporate the card into an existing or new meld/sequence, they MUST take it.
- If a player 'should' take a card (it completes a meld for them) but refuses, opponent may compel them.
- If active player cannot use it, they reject it; opponent may then take it.
- If neither takes it, it goes face-up as a new discard; active player draws top stock card.
- After taking any card, player may rearrange melds on the table, then must discard one card face-up.
Game continues until a player melds all 10 cards (wins) or stock is exhausted (draw).
keyRules: Players' melds are laid face-up on the table throughoutâ€”visible to both.
An opponent can force you to take a card if it fits your existing melds.
Stock exhausted without winner = draw; often a new deal rewards the non-losing player.

strategy.basic: Never meld a card that doesn't also serve multiple melds. Keeping options open is critical with only 10 cards.
strategy.intermediate: Forcing Mechanic: Offer discards that your opponent CAN use (forcing them to take unwanted cards reduces their hand flexibility). Withhold sequences that are close to completionâ€”don't let the opponent see them.
strategy.advanced: Full Sequence Planning: With only 40 cards and melds visible, calculate which cards remain in stock. The endgame is a pure logic puzzleâ€”force your opponent into a position where every stock card improves only your position.
tips: Discard cards that DON'T fit your opponent's visible melds.
Once you have two complete melds (6 cards placed), you need only 1 more meld (3-4 cards) to win.
